text:
maya: heads-up — trying to bring up a HF checkpoint (custom/chat model) into the Redwood conversion pipeline and running into a few things: the model's config.json uses `auto_map` and a custom architecture class, and the tokenizer has nonstandard special tokens (e.g. `<|system|>`). conversion fails unless I set `trust_remote_code=True`, which we can't do in hosted conversion.

jun: can you paste the relevant bits of config.json and tokenizer.json?

maya: sure, excerpt: ```
{
  "architectures": ["CustomChatModel"],
  "auto_map": {"AutoModelForCausalLM": "modeling.custom_model.CustomChatModel"},
  "model_type": "custom_chat"
}
```

and tokenizer special tokens: ```
{
  "special_tokens_map": {"bos_token": "<|system|>", "eos_token": "<|end|>"},
  "added_tokens": ["<|user|>", "<|assistant|>"]
}
```

leo: classic trust_remote_code case. Our HF converter can't execute remote code so auto_map breaks import. Also tokenizer special tokens map to chat templates that our runtime expects as `<s>`/`</s>` etc.

sam: what happens if you vendor the custom code into the conversion tool? any security concerns?

maya: we tried vendoring a minimal shim (implemented CustomChatModel inheriting from GPT2LMHeadModel and mapping forward), converter succeeded, but then quantized the model (bnb 8-bit) and saw a regression on LAMBADA and our internal chat-eval prompts: baseline (HF native, no conversion) LAMBADA acc=62.1%, converted+quantized acc=58.4%.

priya: did you check tokenizer ids mapping? sometimes special tokens get new ids after conversion and prefixes break prompt parsing.

maya: yep — found that `<|system|>` ended up as an added token id at the end, not as bos_token_id, so the chat template used by the app was inserting `<s>` instead of `<|system|>`. patched tokenizer.json to set `bos_token` to `<|system|>` and wrote a small migration: `tokenizer.bos_token = '<|system|>'; tokenizer.add_special_tokens(...)`. After repacking and rerunning quantization, LAMBADA improved to 61.7% (still small gap).

jun: ok progress. two orthogonal problems: 1) auto_map/trust_remote_code, 2) tokenizer special tokens + chat template mismatch. For (1) long-term we should support a safer shim system so that converters can map custom classes to builtin architectures without executing arbitrary code.

leo: proposal: during conversion, if `auto_map` present, require a metadata file `redwood_compat.json` alongside the repo with a safe `auto_map_shims` mapping, e.g.: ```
{
  "auto_map_shims": {"modeling.custom_model.CustomChatModel": "gpt2.GPT2LMHeadModel"},
  "notes": "shim maps custom architectures to known HF classes for loading without trust_remote_code"
}
```
This gives us deterministic loading and avoids executing remote code.

priya: +1. also include a test harness that asserts equivalence on a small set of prompts (sanity-check logits) so we catch large divergences after quantization.

maya: we added a small unit that compares top-1 token for 50 prompts. that caught a case where layernorm eps differences (custom config had eps=1e-6 vs default 1e-5) caused token-level drift after 8-bit quant. changing eps back to 1e-6 in the converted config fixed most divergence.

sam: notes for the conversion docs: - look for `auto_map` and fail with an actionable error linking to `redwood_compat.json` template - validate tokenizer special tokens are set and that chat templates map to those tokens - run a lightweight regression harness pre/post quant - expose a `--allow-trust-remote-code` flag for on-prem conversions only (with clear warnings)

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: conversion pipeline changes merged to `eng-ml/convert-shims` branch. CI will run 50 prompt equivalence test and a quick LAMBADA pass.

leo: one more gotcha — some HF repos use `AddedToken` objects and custom normalization; those don't serialize cleanly into `tokenizer.json`. converter should detect `added_tokens` entries that are objects and flatten them to string tokens + save `added_tokens_special_flags.json` metadata so loaders can reconstruct behavior if the user supplies a shim module.

maya: thanks everyone. next steps: i'll open a PR to add the `redwood_compat.json` template, add the tokenizer validation step, and paste failing prompts into the PR for easier review.

sam: if you want I can pair on the quant test harness tomorrow.

maya: appreciate it — ping me when you have 30m. :thumbsup:

leo: and log this thread in the onboarding playbook under "HF-to-Redwood conversion gotchas" so PMs know to ask for these artifacts before scheduled bringups.

priya: leaving a short checklist for the PR: 1) fail fast on auto_map w/out shim 2) tokenizer special token validator 3) small equivalence test (50 prompts) 4) docs and example redwood_compat.json 5) note about layernorm eps/quant sensitivity

maya: added to PR description. thanks all!
